scope: SHRESTA EXCLUSIVE saree-focused premium quick commerce backend
nonNegotiables: All money is stored and transported as BIGINT paise. Never float, double, decimal string, or rupees for internal money.
All persistent primary keys are UUID v4 generated by PostgreSQL gen_random_uuid(). Never integer auto-increment.
Domain events that trigger async work are published only after transaction commit.
Frontend must not own category, storefront, product, or asset datasets. These come from backend APIs and PostgreSQL-owned configuration.
Media originals are stored separately from generated variants. Backend responses expose S3-compatible versioned/cache-busted URLs, versions, dimensions, LQIP, and srcset-ready variants.
Image binaries are not allowed under backend runtime source/resources. Repository image files may live only under seed/shresta-media as object-storage seed input.
Spring Boot must not serve /shresta-media or /shresta-assets; customer/admin image URLs must be built from object keys and the configured S3-compatible public media base.
Phase 1 cart state is Redis-primary. Do not create PostgreSQL cart tables in Phase 1.
Razorpay webhook is the payment source of truth. Frontend callbacks are user-experience hints only.
Warehouse and delivery zone are resolved when an address is saved, not during checkout.

SHRESTA is quick-commerce first; backend order, store, logistics, and support APIs must model customer-facing delivery promises in minutes, hours, or same-day slots instead of multi-day ecommerce shipping defaults.
Order items are immutable frozen snapshots of product SKU, slug, name, family, type, unit price in paise, line price in paise, and media metadata.
.ai documentation is updated in the same change as any source, schema, API, dependency, infra, or config change.
Every significant Java class has a sibling .ai-context.json before the class is considered complete.
All mutating admin APIs require Idempotency-Key handling and Redis-backed mutation locking.
Admin ACL has four roles only: SUPER_ADMIN, CHANGE_SUBMITTER, CHANGE_REVIEWER, and CHANGE_MANAGER.
Admin create/update/archive/delete work must be represented as a persisted change request before reviewer approval.
Reviewer approval applies the approved payload in the same backend transaction before the change request is marked APPROVED.
KV-first reads are configurable by table. PostgreSQL remains durable truth, and KV is refreshed only after transaction commit.
UAT login seed data is allowed only through local, dev, or UAT Flyway locations. Production must not load db/dev-uat-migration.
Storefront collection counts must be computed from backend product-card rows, not hard-coded frontend values or stale collection metadata.
Any storefront collection may use metadata.productBadgeFilters; backend counting and frontend inclusion must use the same generic normalized badge-token logic without slug-specific exceptions.
Storefront product cards must expose customer-facing description and longDescription from PostgreSQL so PDP text is backend-owned and admin-editable.
Customer-visible storefront/store seed copy must not mention backend, API, DB/KV, S3/CDN, metadata, contracts, snapshots, or other implementation terms.
Proceed-to-checkout must create or reuse a backend customer_order_drafts checkout order ID for the authenticated customer and exact normalized cart signature; the draft is valid for 15 minutes.
Any changed-cart proceed-to-checkout attempt must invalidate older ACTIVE drafts for that customer before creating the new checkout order ID.
Final customer order placement must include draftOrderId and convert an ACTIVE, unexpired, cart-matched draft in the same transaction as order persistence.
Customer order placement requires bearer customer session authentication, Idempotency-Key handling, and mutation locking; browser-submitted prices or totals are never trusted.

Customer order summaries and detail reads are always filtered by customer_orders.customer_id from the authenticated session, so email and phone identities mapped to one customerId share one order history.

phaseOneOperatingModel.cache: Redis 7 for cart, OTP, idempotency, reservations, sessions, and low-latency read snapshots
phaseOneOperatingModel.events: Spring ApplicationEventPublisher with after-commit listeners and stable event contracts
phaseOneOperatingModel.search: PostgreSQL full-text search and pg_trgm before Typesense
phaseOneOperatingModel.infrastructure: Railway.app for launch, with direct migration paths to AWS ECS Fargate

categoryFoundation.apiFacetFormat: lowercase snake_case key:value strings such as metal_colour:rose_gold and silk_type:kanchipuram
categoryFoundation.rule: Catalog, search, tax, analytics, admin, and recommendation logic must read category configuration; do not hard-code saree-only assumptions.

rules: Store originals separately from generated optimized variants.
Generate thumbnail, small, medium, and large variants for uploaded images.
Existing asset image replacement preserves assetKey, writes a new versioned object key, regenerates variants/LQIP, and bumps the asset version.
Admin-managed media asset tags must normalize to uppercase token values, allow only A-Z, 0-9, hyphen, and underscore, and stay within 40 characters per tag and 16 tags per asset.
Generate WebP and AVIF when local/cloud processors support them.
Expose LQIP, byte sizes, optimization stats, backend-built S3-compatible URLs, and long-cache-compatible object paths.
Admin asset search must handle empty filters without PostgreSQL parameter inference failures.
Archive/remove hides records from active APIs; hard purge must be a separate guarded operation.

mutationSafety.writeFlow: lock -> DB transaction -> after-commit KV publish -> idempotency replay record
rules: Same idempotency key plus same request payload returns the stored response.
Same idempotency key plus different request payload returns IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_CONFLICT.
Concurrent protected writes return MUTATION_LOCKED instead of overwriting each other.

adminGovernance.rule: ARCHIVE is temporary removal; DELETE is permanent row removal and must be a separately reviewed request.
